#4288. Barbie Rewind Review: A Treasure Trove of Classic Barbie Video Games

Barbie returns with a spectacular collection of 16 classic, retro games, including an unreleased title, to celebrate her nearly 70-year history.

For almost 70 years, Barbie has dominated the toy industry and pop culture in ways that are almost unfathomable. After watching her daughter play with paper dolls and assign them adult roles and lives, Ruth Handler convinced her husband Elliot to start creating dolls that broke away from the usual infant or toddler designs.

They named her Barbie after their daughter Barbara, launching what would become one of the most iconic pop culture icons of all time. As any good pop culture landmark does, Barbie eventually started making her way into video games. I’m a bit of a Barbie fanatic, and I suspect one of the main reasons for that is playing Barbie video games during a lot of the 1990s.

TMNT fans are in for a real treat with Digital Eclipse's retro compilation of classic games.

To celebrate the rich longevity of the legendary doll, Digital Eclipse and Atari have teamed up to produce Barbie Rewind. This spectacular collection brings together 12 of Barbie’s most beloved games, all of them packed together in what has become a rather common feat for Digital Eclipse. This celebratory package of Barbie’s endearing legacy of empowerment is one that every fan of the iconic doll is going to want to add to their dream home.

Barbie Rewind uses a really fun framing device to sort of justify the existence of the games in the collection. That was entirely optional, and Digital Eclipse didn’t have to actually do that, but what they’ve done is incredibly cute. Normally, games just exist in a collection and that’s it, but Barbie Rewind makes a direct effort to explain why all these games are together.

In the “Let’s Decorate” mode, you are tasked with designing a Barbie Dream Home with assistance from Barbie herself. In order to unlock more stuff for the house, you have to play the games in the collection. It’s a fun little incentive to get you playing more of the collection, which helps keep the game from feeling like a museum, and instead infuses it with the classic Barbie personality.

Like so many of Digital Eclipse’s previous collections, Barbie Rewind is built around a genuine love for the IP it’s celebrating. Though it sadly lacks some of the more comprehensive video documentaries and historical documentation that have made previous Digital Eclipse collections even more engaging, there’s still a lot to love here as a Barbie fan.

Each game does include beautiful scans of the manual, and the lack of video documentaries isn’t exactly the worst thing in the world, but after seeing the effort that was put into them from previous collections, them not being here in some form is a bit disappointing. Even so, there are a grand total of 16 Barbie games here, even including an unreleased game known as Barbie: Vacation Adventure, so there’s quite a lot of content to sort through here.

The Blue Bomber is back once again in this underwhelming collection of DS games.

Among the 16 Barbie games included with Barbie Rewind, so many of them hit me in ways that I wasn’t quite expecting. Growing up loving Barbie was one thing, but aside from the unreleased game, which I wasn’t aware of until this collection came around, I have strong, distinct memories from each title in the collection. It’s been quite an experience to explore these games again.

Beginning with a game known simply as Barbie that released on the NES in 1991, Barbie Rewind chronicles her outstanding run of video games all the way through the SNES and the PS1, all the way up to the GBA in 2007. Through nearly two decades of Barbie video games, Digital Eclipse has done a fabulous job of bringing so many iconic games back to the forefront.

Like so many of Digital Eclipse’s previous collections, Barbie Rewind is built around a genuine love for the IP it’s celebrating.

These games come from a very different time in not just video game history, but Barbie’s history as well. Barbie was continuously built on making sure girls knew they could be literally anything they wanted, whether that was a world champion rollerblader or a detective. It often feels like some sort of bizarre mash-up of WarioWare and Barbie, as you’ll go from designing a dream home to being a secret agent.

Many of the games are also charmingly bite-sized in their minute-to-minute gameplay, so you can seamlessly jump between each game to your heart’s content. Like a lot of retro collections, Barbie Rewind also has a rewind feature, but the buttons for that rewind feature also tend to pop off and on randomly at the beginning of each game in some rather annoying ways. It isn’t an outright disaster, but it was enough to get rather irritating after a while.

While Barbie has dominated TV and movies, including a big budget blockbuster adaptation in 2023 starring Margot Robbie, one of her more successful ventures over the years has been video games. Each decade of Barbie has seen her try her hand at everything from being an astronaut to a rock star, leaning heavily into the pop culture that defined that era.

The games in Barbie Rewind are indicative of that, as well. If you grew up with Chris Anthony, Mattel’s very own in-house voice of Barbie for over a decade, as the voice of Barbie, you’ll be right at home. Many of these games, such as Barbie: Race & Ride and The Barbie Diaries, are intrinsically tied to a very specific era of the character.

Super Bomberman Collection celebrates the legacy of one of Konami's best franchises in this outstanding compilation. Here's our full review.

It often feels like some sort of bizarre mash-up of WarioWare and Barbie, as you’ll go from designing a dream home to being a secret agent.

They feel like time capsules, and revisiting them in this collection is going to be an absolute delight for anyone who grew up with this wonderful time for her. This was right at the height of Mattel figuring out that Barbie needed to be and feel more connected to the young people who collected her toys. You can still feel some essence of Barbie’s previous life in the early games, but as each new title comes along, you’ll notice a distinct evolution that’s impossible to ignore.

Though the games in the collection vary in quality, all of them are worth jumping into in their own unique ways. The early platformers are all fairly basic, although some of them actually have fun physics that felt unique for the time, but the real draw is in the later PS1 and Game Boy games. You never really know what each game is going to throw at you, and for a character who made her name on being anything she wanted to be, that feels quite in character for the ambitious woman they call Barbie.

Barbie Rewind brings together 16 classic Barbie games, including an unreleased Genesis and SNES game, for one spectacularly nostalgic package. The quality of each game is wildly different, but that tends to come with the territory of these retro collections. Each game feels uniquely fun in its own way, but the package itself has a strange issue with the rewind buttons, as well as a lack of video documentaries that have defined previous Digital Eclipse collections.

It’s a logistics puzzler that’s out now on iPhone.

The map starts under a thick Fog. Just like London has been the past few days. You put up Scout Towers to burn it back in bursts, and each surge reveals lost Buildings that need to be brought back. For that, you need the right resources, which must be hauled around by Trundlers along conveyor routes you lay yourself. And if a mountain gets in your way, just blow it up.

Crafting runs from Rubble at the bottom to the Boom Core at the top, across sixteen resources, six tiers and 26 kinds of Building. Gobs from nearby Gob Camps can speed a building up or carry resources from places your routes haven’t reached yet. The maps are procedurally generated too, with roughly 281 quadrillion possible layouts.

Factory games like these make you live with your mistakes. A messy layout tends to stay messy. Gobs & Gear makes rebuilding the point. I’d say Mini Motorways is the nearest relative, where half the time you’re pulling up the road you placed five minutes ago.

There’s no grinding between runs and no punishing timers either. Given the Gob King’s mood, I thought there’d be a timer. It’s all pixel art, and the building names do a fair bit of the joking, the Smelty Hole and the Dig Pit among them.

Gobs & Gears is out today on iOS for a one-off $9.99 purchase.

If you’d prefer puzzles with fewer explosions, our list of the best strategy games on iOS is mostly bomb-free.

Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.

The first new arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden. Columbina is a 5-Star Hydro Catalyst wielder. Her kit revolves around supporting the squad via Lunar Reactions. She can trigger coordinated Lunar Reaction DMG, even when she’s off the field.

The Moon Maiden’s special ability, Lunar Domain, further boosts all Lunar Reactions by applying a DMG bonus, including summoning more thundercloud strikes for Lunar-Charged reactions. Speaking of elemental reactions, new in this version is Lunar-Crystallize, a new reaction that’s triggered when Geo meets Hydro (under certain conditions). Then there’s Zibai, an Adeptus from Liyue. Zibai is another 5-Star character, a Geo Sword wielder. Zibai can, through entering a special state where they can build up energy, unleash an Elemental Skill that deals Lunar-Crystallize DMG.

The second phase’s rerun will be Neuvillette, who’s also going to have a new outfit in the shop at a discount.

Version Luna 4 brings back the annual Lantern Rite event, taking place in the mainland of Liyue. The event features its own set of minigames with unique rewards, alongside new stories of the Adepti.

All around Liyue Harbor, you’ll be able to place Xiao Lanterns and inscribe them with messages for others to read. You’ll also earn some Fortune Coins from Auspicious Treasure Trees, which you can later exchange for gifts.

All players will receive 1,600 Primogems through the in-game mail. If you log in regularly, you can earn up to ten Intertwined Fates. Lantern Rite has a new outfit for Yaoyao, which is also where you have a chance to earn one 4-Star Liyue character for free.

Finally, you can look forward to the new Classic Mode in Miliastra Wonderland, which lets you invite select Teyvat characters to join you.

#4277. Diablo 4's long-awaited Tower and its Leaderboards enter beta today, and there's no PTR funny business this time

Diablo 4's first big moment of 2026 is nearly upon us, and it's one feature many have been looking forward to for actual years.

Diablo 4 is about to deliver on Blizzard’s years-old promise to add a challenging, leaderboard-driven experience to the action RPG. The beta for The Tower, and its associated Leaderboards are about to kick off.

As recently revealed, the new experience launches today at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT. This is a beta version that arrives alongside update 2.5.2.

This early launch won’t offer the full experience, and it’s mainly designed to get it into the hands of players early so that Blizzard could get as much feedback as possible and incorporate it into the final version.

The beta is available to everyone, which is a nice change from the usual rigmarole players would have to go through to get the PTR build and play on a different branch. The Tower, and Leaderboards will be available only in the Seasonal Realm, however. Indeed, the plan is to build on what’s there with each future season, so it’s best to think of it as a seasonal experience.

The Tower is about as simple of an activity as you can get in an action RPG. The goal is to climb as many floors as you can as quickly as you can, all while battling increasingly difficult mobs.

You need to reach and beat the Tower’s final boss before you can call it a run. The Leaderboard will then show your time, and let you see how well you did compared to other players.

The Tower is available to anyone who completed Rank 2 of the current Season Rank. Once done, an Obelisk will appear in Cerrigar, letting you access the challenge.

The Leaderboards themselves will operate on a two-week schedule, all of which will take place during a given season. In this case, they’re going to close the day before Season of the Divine Interversion - the game’s current season - ends.

Blizzard published an updated set of patch notes that show how much has changed since The Tower, and Leaderboards first became playable in the patch 2.5.0 PTR.

Though the two new additions have been anticipated for a while, there’s not been much exciting going on in the world of Diablo 4, apart, of course, from the surprise arrival of The Paladin class, which became available in December last year to coincide with the announcement of Lord of Hatred, the game’s next expansion.

#4273. Jordan Esports Federation signs MoU with King Hussein Business Park to host more events

Priya Venkatesh has been following the money in esports since before brand deals were considered legitimate marketing. She got pulled into the scene through competitive fighting games and eventually found herself more interested in the contracts and partnerships behind the tournaments than the matches themselves. These days she focuses on how brands navigate esports sponsorships, where the smart money is going, and which deals are actually built to last versus the ones that look good in a press release.

The Jordan Esports Federation (JEF) has signed a memorandum of understanding with King Hussein Business Park (KHBP) in Amman, giving the national body a formal framework to stage more tournaments and events at the site it already calls home.

KHBP announced the deal on Sunday in a statement published on its website. Prince Omar bin Faisal, who is President of the JEF, attended the signing.

Under the MoU, the federation and the business park will jointly host and organise specialised competitions on the KHBP campus. They will also receive the international delegations and official guests that travel to those events. Beyond the competitive side, the two organisations plan to cooperate on media and marketing, look at shared education, training and community projects, and swap knowledge and expertise.

Neither party has disclosed financial terms or the length of the agreement.

KHBP CEO Eng. Ammar Ezzeddin presented the MoU as part of the park’s wider ambitions. “This partnership builds on our ongoing efforts to create an enabling environment for institutions, initiatives and high-potential sectors, and to establish KHBP as a hub for innovation and technology,” he said.

He added: “We look forward to helping the sector thrive and to hosting more tournaments and events that put Jordanian talent in the spotlight and raise the Kingdom’s profile in this field.”

JEF Vice President Hazem Bawab focused on the competitive and grassroots goals. “This partnership is a significant step in our drive to develop the esports industry in Jordan and elevate the standard of local, regional and international competitions and activities,” he said.

Bawab continued: “We look forward to drawing on the setup and capabilities that KHBP offers to scale our work, nurture young talent and launch joint programmes that help the industry grow and encourage greater participation.”

The deal formalises a relationship that already exists on the ground. According to The Esports Radar, the JEF, which is the government recognised regulator for esports in the country, is based at the park in West Amman.

A lot of that work happens at THE ARC, the arena and gaming dome inside the park. The same report lists past events there including the fourth Arab Esports League, a Women’s Esports Championship and Red Bull Login, which doubled as Jordan’s national final stage in Dota 2 and Counter-Strike 2. The venue is also an incubation centre supported by the federation and the Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship, and runs training camps for players hoping to turn professional.

KHBP has been a destination for esports investment for some time. In 2024, lounge operator True Gamers announced plans for an esports venue in Jordan at the business park, a project in which its CPO publicly thanked the JEF and Prince Omar.

The timing also puts Amman in the industry spotlight. PocketGamer.biz points out that Pocket Gamer Connects Jordan takes place on 7 and 8 November, bringing many of the region’s games industry stakeholders to the city later this week.

#4272. The Sims developer vows "our values are unchanged," as it teases multiple projects from post-Saudi-owned EA

The team behind one of EA's most diverse franchises has issued a statement about its future under the soon-to-be Saudi-owned publisher.

In their (slightly belated) new years message to players, the developer of EA’s The Sims series of games has lightly addressed concerns about its future within the publisher in a wide-ranging letter to the community.

The letter also serves as something of a light plan for what players can expect soon, and in the future, alongside what the various teams are currently working on.

The developer starts off the yearly check-in with a statement that attempts to address concerns about the future of The Sims, historically one of EA’s most inclusive and culturally diverse franchises.

This, of course, comes in the wake of last year’s bombshell that EA is being taken private by a coalition led by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), alongside investment firms Silver Lake Capital and Affinity Partners. The $55 billion acquisition was approved by EA’s shareholders in December, and is set to close by the end of June.

Understandably, many raised concerns about what EA’s new ownership would mean for its people, and portfolio of games. The news is concerning for The Sims in particular, a series that’s long embraced diversity and inclusivity, and has historically been popular among women, people of colour, and members of the LGBTQ+ community.

“Our Sims team's creative control, guided by our values of inclusivity, choice, creativity, community, and play, has not changed,” the post reads, though without referring to the buyout directly at any point.

“These values inspire the decisions we make each and every day as we plan for today, tomorrow, and the future.”

As for what’s to come in 2026 and beyond, it sounds like The Sims team has multiple irons in the fire. The developer is working on “a family of new Sims experiences” that will find homes on PC, console, and mobile. Crucially, the post says that not every experience will be on every platform, in order for each to focus on delivering something different and interesting.

Future releases, of course, include new The Sims 4 content that focuses on the single-player experience. The social and more multiplayer-driven experiences, however, will instead be found in Project Rene, the mobile-first life-sim currently in development. (Despite early confidence that it was a working title for The Sims 5, it's now confirmed that Project Rene won’t, in fact, be a direct successor to The Sims 4.)

Some of these projects will see more playtesting throughout 2026, so you should probably sign up for The Sims Labs if you want to hear about when/how you can get involved.

#4270. Afterwords – Marvel’s Wolverine

We interviewed game director Mike Daly after the launch of Insomniac’s recent Wolverine game to get his take on what makes Wolverine and Spidey different to work on, his thoughts on breadcrumb trails, and why Logan can’t ever seem to get the girl.

Insomniac had extensive experience working on well-known superhero characters before starting on Wolverine. Early on, what traits or qualities of Logan as a story character and playable avatar did you know you wanted to focus on, distinct from the Spider-Man games and character?

From a story perspective, we wanted Logan to be a man with centuries of experiences that he can’t remember, creating a mix of being worn, wizened, and cynical. His resilience makes him fearless, which comes through in his candid manner, and he can’t ignore his sense of justice, as much as he would like to.

For gameplay, it was important that players felt the difference made by his healing factor, claws, berserker rage, animalistic strength, enhanced senses, his adamantium skeleton, and corresponding weight.

In both story and gameplay, emotionally and physically, Wolverine is a hero who gets hurt and feels that pain deeply but always gets back up again and presses on. This dogged resilience was really important to us and a central theme of story and gameplay.

Wolverine is more of a linear adventure than the open-world exploration of a big city seen in Spidey. In my playthrough, that added to the sense of relentless pacing that characterizes Wolverine as a fictional lead. Was that part of the thinking behind why the game was built that way, or was the more linear path there for other reasons?

Ultimately, we made a game suited for a Wolverine story that had comic book pacing – action and meaningful story development on every page.

We experimented with different structures and stories, evaluating from the perspective of: “Is this the best way to do Wolverine justice?” As the various things we tried didn’t feel right, we had to challenge our assumptions and look to our favorite Wolverine stories for inspiration, which led us to where we ended up – a story with momentum in which every beat felt authentic to the character.

Scenes and gameplay sequences that might have been fine in other games but didn’t strongly evoke Wolverine undermined the consistency of the fantasy we were trying to create, so we tried to keep things very focused.

After the game’s release, there was an active online conversation about some of the breadcrumb-trail guidance the game offers to lead you to pickups, or to mark the continued golden path of progression. What was the thinking internally about that design decision, and your take on the debate after the game launched?

Our thinking was that it was essential to make the player feel like they were empowered by Logan’s enhanced senses, a canonical mutant ability, enabling players to do things they could not with other characters. We wanted to weave that power into as many parts of the game as we could, so that if Logan could smell or hear something relevant, the player could see it too.

For collectibles, we wanted players to enjoy seeking out and spotting senses cues, enabling you to find things that would have been obscure to other characters. Using the cues, players can cover a lot of ground without feeling the need to scour, maintaining story and action momentum.

After the game launched, we saw feedback from players that interpreted senses as abstract designer guidance, along with a desire for options in how they approached exploration and discovery. Fortunately, we have been able to incorporate this feedback from players in our post-launch patches. One aspect we’ve improved is the scent trail’s organic presentation, so they give a stronger impression that they belong in the world rather than being an abstraction. For players that want to do more manual exploration, we’ve added options to remove the sense cues for optional collectibles, and one to make scent trails dimmer until the player requests a hint.

Ultimately, enhanced senses are still essential to creating an authentic Wolverine, and that’s still reflected in the cinematic and environmental storytelling of the game. I think it’s great that on top of that, players now have more flexibility in how they experience them.

As a longtime comics fan, I found Logan’s combat system especially exciting, particularly for the relentless forward momentum it provided. What do you think were some of the keys to nailing that dynamic, as distinct from other high-quality third-person action games?

There were a few key elements we wanted to get right - Logan’s resilience, rage, claw feel, and overall lethality.

For resilience, Logan’s healing factor needed to feel important for survival - a prominent element of the system. A natural starting point there was to try continual regeneration so you could outlast enemies, but that quickly fell apart as it incentivized the player to slow the pace of combat or even retreat for maximum advantage. Even though it was incredibly effective at enabling survival, it was also hard to notice by the player so it didn’t feel prominent.

The key to solving this problem was making a connection between rage and healing factor. The Last Stand mechanic is a healing surge that can happen when you lose all your health, themed as using adrenaline to keep Logan’s heart beating. This incentivized aggression and made a space for an up-close look at visceral healing.

Speaking of rage, it’s the backbone of the combat system where being an indicator of momentum is key. At the low end of rage, you don’t have the safety net of Last Stand, so your decision-making naturally biases towards survival; ensuring you prioritize threat assessment and defense. As you climb into the middle tier, you have the leeway to push your luck for longer combos or barrages that let you build up rage and get kills faster. Finally, you get to rage tier 3, where the quick decay of rage makes your rate of kills the top priority, so you might prefer to attack groups over ranged stragglers just for the improved kill density. Beyond the mechanics, we change the presentation of combat, especially through Logan’s animations and exertion to reflect his state of mind. The presentation and systemic incentives drive the player into a frenzy, just like Wolverine.

We invested a lot in the details of claw feel to make sure it was distinct from general game attacks. Claws shred, so we added locational body damage to our enemies to reflect that, along with a dynamic blood system where it globs together as it is spilled, splatters on contact with characters or the environment, drips down the walls, diffuses in the water, and other details. Many kills throughout combat are punctuated with custom animations with cinematic camera work that pushes in and frames the puncturing of claws into the body for a strong impression of the connection and weight of the puncture. Severing limbs on these attacks is an occasional reminder of how sharp Logan’s adamantium claws are. Reinforcing this is top-notch sound and haptics design, so each hit registers.

The last aspect I’ll touch on is lethality, the rate at which Wolverine is able to dispatch enemies and vice versa. We found that fights where enemies were more technical and could survive a lot undermined what players expected to experience as Wolverine, which was aggressively and lethally tearing through a lot of enemies. On the other hand, combat was less exciting if the enemies didn’t feel like a serious and deadly threat, and you didn’t feel like Wolverine if a little bit of caution could enable you to defend perfectly and avoid all damage.

These aspects led us towards encounters where you confronted large groups of enemies that were highly aggressive, to the point of feeling unfair. Enemies can’t believably go toe-to-toe with Wolverine alone, even world-class mercenaries, so their strategy is in group coordination, which creates a counterweight to Wolverine’s own rage-based momentum.

Marvel’s Wolverine draws in a number of characters from across the X-Men comic mythology, but notably makes no mention of some foundational figures of that fiction – Professor Xavier and Magneto. That, in turn, leads to dramatically different lives for characters like Jean Grey or Logan. Is the narrative you crafted an intentional exploration of a world where those figures weren’t present in the early days of mutant emergence?

I would say it was more of an exploration of the character than the world. We wanted a story where Logan is pulled into conflict not because he’s a crusader, but because there’s no other option. There are no X-Men to help. His growth as a person should be a challenging journey, which could go unearned if he was surrounded by wise, supportive, heroic characters pushing him in the right direction. In contrast, his dynamic with the members of Team X evokes his struggle. The adversity to personal growth is what makes it interesting.

Jean does end up being the person that pushes him in the right direction, and that works because they can relate to each other, having had similar struggles.

In several versions of Marvel storytelling, Jean and Logan share a special bond, but Jean ultimately chooses Scott Summers as a partner. But even without that barrier in your story, Logan still hits some roadblocks to love. Is Wolverine fundamentally a better character when he just can’t get the girl?

The way I would put it is that a Wolverine story is fundamentally better when you empathize with Logan’s pain and admire him for pressing on despite it. That goes for his emotional pain as much as physical. He’s a tragic character in this regard – all he wants is to be at peace but can never find it for long.

Wolverine gets to take on a lot of the “heavy hitters” of his comic mythology in different boss fights throughout the game. When you began development, do you recall who the very first character was that you decided he simply had to fight in your game?

Sabretooth. No character is a better foil for Logan. His inner turmoil and chaotic behavior helps illustrate Logan’s own inner beast and his struggle to resist it. Sabretooth’s strength and mutant powers also provide a mirror to Logan in combat, and his savagery creates shocking moments that leave an impression. We knew an epic confrontation with Sabretooth was going to be a thing from the start.

#4269. The Sims 4 gets a bunch of free items inspired by Coach that you can use right now

As part of a free update, The Sims 4 has kicked off a new collaboration with Coach, which means there's free stuff for everyone.

The Sims 4’s first update of the year is here, though it may not be quite what you might have expected. The game’s latest patch mainly centres around a collaboration with Coach, the luxury fashion brand.

This obviously isn’t the game’s first collaboration with a known brand, though this one does include a lot of free items and accessories that anyone can make use of, even if they don’t care about Coach.

The Coach Collection brings nine new items to The Sims 4. They range from clothes and accessories you can use with Create a Sim, to decoration items available in Build Buy. There’s also The Carriage House, a new Gallery household where you can find three new roommates.

There’s a nice bit of variety in the options available, some casual and others more practical for your Sims to wear. Then there’s The Bag Room, which can also be grabbed from the Gallery. The room simply serves as a way for you to show off your Coach bags and trunks collection.

In case you missed it, The Sims’ development team recently shared an update on some of what we can expect in 2026, both for The Sims 4 as well as other projects currently in the works. It even included further confirmation, if any was needed, that Project Rene is a dedicated mobile off-shoot, and not — as many had long believed — The Sims 5.

The blog post also included a statement about EA’s imminent change of ownership, which many fear could alter the series’ inclusive and diverse nature, and the decisions made by its various teams.

#4268. Battlefield 6 Season 2 delayed like many of us expected, but we're getting a new update and a bonus battle pass path

Battlefield 6 has pushed back its next season by nearly a month in order to refine Season 2 content and implement more of players' feedback.

Battlefield Studios has released its first official communication in 2026. Rather than unveil the second season of Battlefield 6, however, the developer instead announced a delay. The currently ongoing Season 1 was initially meant to end on Tuesday, January 20, hence why the developer had to communicate something this week.

Season 1 will now end on Tuesday, February 17, which is also when Season 2 will kick off. Given the current sentiment around the game, this news isn’t surprising in the least.

In the blog post announcing the delay, BF Studios said that the decision to extend the current season and push back the start of the next one allows for extra time to “further polish and refine” Season 2 content.

The developer did not offer any hints about Season 2, but there’s an incredibly brief teaser trailer featuring a soldier wearing a gas mask emerging from an environment drenched in toxic gas.

Given that Battlefield 6’s battle royale mode Redsec does not utilise the popular encroaching gas mechanic (using an encroaching ring of fire instead), it’s possible that we may be looking at something new in multiplayer akin to Battlefield 1. Of course, this may just be a visual piece that doesn’t reflect the gameplay of Season 2.

Escalating the fight with new threats on the battlefield.Season 2 begins February 17. pic.twitter.com/fGMegJJuTj

What we are getting news of today, however, is the game’s next patch. This extension update is going to arrive next week, on January 20, when Season 1 was supposed to end. It’s bringing new weekly challenges to the game, but its biggest addition is yet another Bonus Path to the battle pass. You can also expect the free daily login rewards to continue, alongside other periods of double XP.

Similar to other Bonus Paths, the new Frostfire Bonus Path can be completed alongside the Season 1 battle pass. You’ll need 110 Bonus Path Points in total if you want to earn everything it has to offer, with each tier requiring 10 points. It is worth noting, however, that Frostfire Points are only earned through weekly challenges, meaning there won’t be any bonus challenges associated with it.

Frostfire includes several new customisation rewards, of course, such as a Weapon Package, soldier skin, XP boosts and the usual run of unlocks.

Though the latest blog post may be devoid of any real details on Season 2, BF Studios confirmed that Battlefield Labs will play a larger role in offering a preview of what’s to come, so it’s entirely possible that the testing initiative will soon open its doors to players with an early look at some of the maps and other content planned for Season 2.

#4267. Holiday Gift Guide 2026

With the holiday gift-giving season upon us, it’s time to think about the gaming fans in your life and find the ideal present to brighten their day. And if you’re the gamer in the family, we always encourage you to circle relevant items in the coming pages and leave your magazine open in hard-to-miss locations around the house. We’ve scoured dozens of tech products, tabletop games, collectibles, and more to select and highlight some of the coolest items we found this year.

We recommended the Board shortly after its launch, but with its expanded game library and lower price than first-adopter rates, this holiday season is an ideal time to make the leap. This family-friendly platform features original games that sit comfortably between the digital and physical divide. The horizontally placed screen shows the backdrop of one of the several included games, or the sold-separately add-on games that have popped in since launch. Each game has its own real physical play pieces that interact with the action onscreen, often in innovative and charming ways. Think of it as the best of both worlds between board games and video games, and you’ll get what they’re shooting for here. $399

Few additions to the latest Dungeons & Dragons rules pack as much punch and value as this new expansion, focusing on ways to develop further and evolve the use of magic across your tabletop gaming sessions. New subclasses, spells, creatures, magical items, and factions add thoughtful, intriguing options for both players looking to play someone new and DMs hunting for new story hooks and challenges. $50

If you’re as excited as we are about this month’s celebration of the Tomb Raider legacy (see p. 40), this centerpiece statue is an ideal fit for your collection. Standing roughly nine inches in height, Lara is poised for exploration in her original classic garb. The sculpt strikes a perfect balance between crisp detail and stylistic presentation, in line with that early version of the character; the metallic blue motorcycle paint is especially striking. $250

For players longing for the glory days of stand-up arcade games, it’s hard to beat Arcade 1Up’s approach. The team’s sturdy cabinets look and sound great as a marquee feature of your game room. The new Outrun machine features much of the original display art, a bright 19-inch screen, and responsive gas and brake pedals as you steer around those tight corners. Sega has packed in OutRun, Turbo OutRun, OutRunners, and Power Drift. If old-school racing isn’t your thing, look for cabinets that run the gamut from Pac-Man to Joust to Claw Machines. $629.99

The long-running Nendoroid figures continue to be an attractive but still affordable choice for building collections across numerous fan-favorite series. There are somewhere around 2000 characters at this point! New entries like the Genshin Impact collection make a strong case for the line. The look is chibi, the quality is excellent, poseability is high, and customizable face and accessory parts let you change up your display over time. $46

We’ve previously sung the praises of Libernovo’s versatile approach to an ergonomic gaming chair, which includes a lumbar stretch functionality, a steady recline option for comfortable pushback without sudden shifts, and dynamically adjusting parts as you move through your day. The Maxis line does all that, but addresses one of the fundamental problems for at least some users with the original – it wasn’t big enough. With features like a wider base and longer headrest reach, the Maxis aims to provide the same comfort to the players who are tall or wide enough to need the extra breathing room. $1119

If you’re the player on your team who likes to have easy access to soundboards and real-time voice changing, the Key Pocket could be just the ticket. This small device straps onto your phone for mobile play, but it’s also compatible with consoles, Discord, Twitch, or just about any place you want to tweak audio on the fly. A free tier gives you access to some voice-changing and sounds, while a separate subscription opens up hundreds of thousands of additional options. But be warned: we can’t help you after your friends abandon you for that baby voice you won’t stop using. $99

The question of the best bang for your buck in modern consoles has become extraordinarily complicated, especially as tech prices have soared in recent years. There’s no right answer, but Sony’s high-end machine walks the line of offering extremely high-tier performance without escalating to even higher-priced gaming PCs. Higher and more consistent frame rates than on standard PS5, advanced ray tracing, and an increasing number of games that feature enhanced PSSR image options all add up to a better gaming experience, if you’re ready to make the significant price jump. $900

If the gamer in your life is looking for a stylish, understated way to express their love of the hobby, Anicorn’s designer watch collaboration with PlayStation could be a standout option. Available in black and a slick silver/white combo, the minimalist timepiece includes the familiar face buttons of Sony’s controller encased in an oil-injection display so they slowly and freely float across the watch as you move. $250

It’s a safe bet you’ve at least seen the popular Shashibo puzzle cubes by this point. We’ve been fans of their brain-teasing, fidgety fun for some time. Battle Shapes takes the core concept – reshaping the box into various distinct magnetically-locked shapes – and extends it into a timed game experience, playable solo or head-to-head. By targeting specific shapes, you significantly improve your speed with the toy, and scannable QR codes on the cards offer clear tutorials for each shape so you can prep for competition. $50

While the vast majority of gamers looking for good personal audio are going to be okay with a larger set of cans over their ears, We know more than a few players for whom that’s a definite no – for comfort, awareness of surrounding sounds, or other reasons. The Arc 5 earbuds aim to solve for that, with an over-ear design that feels extremely comfortable. And because they sit on the ear, you can still hear what’s going on around you. While that limits some aspects of the final sound quality, the inclusion of THX certification, Dolby Atmos optimization, and Dynamic Bass Enhancement helps to ensure audio is still very strong. $230

Across Lego’s many recent themes, Tolkien’s legendarium has offered some stellar sets. The largest yet is the capital of Gondor, with an astonishing 8,278 pieces and a height of roughly two feet. The castle/city build is impressive, featuring tons of interesting angles and turns. The finished product aims to offer the best of both worlds in presentation – a microscale representation of the front façade and a reverse minifigure-scale Hall of Kings. We especially like the inclusion of Denethor’s cherry tomatoes. $650

The original Azul is often cited as a foundational entry in modern board gaming. The “Kids” versions of celebrated titles aren’t always a sure bet, but this one holds up to scrutiny. Azul Kids lowers the complexity threshold but keeps the foundational strategic thinking. Players lay out uniquely shaped tiles into mosaic frameworks in colorful, appealing patterns; the basic concept of the original inspiration is clear, and kids as young as five can grasp and enjoy the fun. $25

Many corners of the collecting world have embraced the fun (and frequent despair) of blind boxes, where you never know exactly who you’ll get in a given series. Funism has a strong track record for quality, offering adorable smaller figures like their latest line of Evangelion collectibles. Each figure stands nearly four inches and features both human characters and mecha. You can buy singles and roll the dice, or purchase larger sets with a no-duplicates guarantee, which can save a lot of heartache if you’re trying to line your whole shelf. $21

If you’re going to spring for a high-end keyboard for PC gaming, it’s important that you like the feel of the keys. The slightly smaller overall 75% size profile of this Blackwidow has no impact on the great feel of typing – a clear highlight for the unit. The customizable, colored backlights are also a big selling point, as is the side command dial and built-in OLED display, which can be tweaked to show PC performance, GIFs, lighting brightness, and more. It’s a strong contender in a crowded field, and justifies its price with both comfort and customizability. $300

Beautiful, vibrant art and a refreshing take on the classic area-control board game genre are the two strongest reasons to take a close look at Wroth. Players control one of five races vying for supremacy across a conflict-ridden peninsula. Factions are asymmetric, so everyone has unique capabilities, and that adds significant replayability. Players roll and draft dice, allowing distinct actions that move the game forward. And move it does; unlike many games of this ilk, Wroth can be learned quickly and played to completion in a little over an hour. $65

Console and computer hardware prices are skyrocketing with no sign of slowing, and perhaps as a result, retro gaming handhelds are gaining popularity. Many quality devices are available, but what sets the Evercade Nexus apart is its officially licensed game cartridges. Imagine the nostalgic joy of a Game Boy, but with a cartridge that includes both Banjo-Kazooie and Tooie. The cartridge boxes even include manuals. For fans of physical media, Evercade Nexus is a great option. $199

This tiny USB-C plug-in (with included USB-A adapter) solves a bunch of audio challenges in one uniform device. It offers high-resolution Bluetooth transmission on iPhone, high-bitrate audio transmission to compatible LDAC headphones, enables high-quality Bluetooth output from your PC, and even low-latency Bluetooth audio on PS5 and Switch. In short, it takes a huge number of products with a USB port and ensures a dynamic Bluetooth audio connection with relative ease. $99

The original MV6 is a familiar sight on streams thanks to its clear voice reproduction and overall ease of use. Shure has built on that success with the Gen 2, offering an excellent standalone mic that doesn’t break the bank. Available in black or white, the Gen 2 features a handy auto-level mode that keeps volume even as you adjust your own amplitude, an adjustable denoiser for your space, a longer cable for out-of-the-box convenience, and three presets for plug-and-play use. In short, it’s an excellent choice if you want great performance without needing an audio engineering degree. $169

XR Glasses are still fighting for awareness, but once you try them, it’s easy to see why the concept is on the rise. Viture’s Pro 2 makes an impressive case for adoption, with a competitive price point, comfortable wear, and a giant 146-inch screen that floats in front of your face for gaming or work on your PC or phone. The display is crisp, bright, and impressive, even as the glasses are light and easy to use. With a mobile dock mini (sold separately), you can even snap onto a Switch 2 with ease and start playing instantly. $299

Role-playing gamers have several excellent universal systems to pick between when considering a story or campaign idea that might fall outside traditional genre staples. Among many good options, Cypher stands out as one of the very best. The system uses a rules-light, narrative-focused approach that prioritizes player-driven storytelling across everything from hard sci-fi to superheroes to intrigue- driven espionage. This is the corebook that’s needed to run and play the full system; additional books only add options. $50

As gamers have continually migrated toward personal audio that can rock amazing sound without disturbing the whole house, high-end premium headphones have become a dangerously competitive space. Turtle Beach meets that challenge head-on, with a robust option that sounds beautiful in use. The Stealth Pro II boasts the slick ability to wirelessly switch between different devices, which is awesome if you’re one of those players who regularly jumps between platforms to play your favorite titles. Like the whole category, it’s a lot to spend on a headset, but Dolby Atmos, active noise cancellation, and 60mm dual drivers all add up to a powerful argument. $300

With an increasing number of top-tier console and PC games like Resident Evil Village, No Man’s Sky, and Dead Cells now available on iOS, not to mention the consistent quality of Apple Arcade, Apple phones remain the best mobile platform for gaming. The 18 Pro Max phone has implemented a number of tweaks that strengthen the platform, including higher memory, much faster graphics processing, impressive HDR performance, and notably improved battery life, all adding up to a gaming experience that is working hard to justify your playtime when away from home. Starting at $1299

SteelSeries is best known for its strong audio line-up, but its push into premium-tier controllers exhibits a similar flair for quality and usability. The new Aeon Pro has a lot to recommend it as your go-to Xbox, PC, or mobile choice. The two included batteries (one of which can always be charging in the dock) ensure essentially unlimited playtime. The full-pull or hair triggers and buttons are clicky and satisfying, and the Hall Effect thumbsticks are built to minimize any drift. Textured handgrips and overall heft are ideal. And an onboard OLED lets you adjust profiles and button assignments, switch between platforms, and check battery at a glance. $260

Valve’s pricey VR headset isn’t a revolution in the medium, but the company has been invested in the technology since its inception. As a result, the Steam Frame is a very good, very comfortable headset. Like its competition, the Quest, its best use is playing games locally on the headset, and Steam’s library is vast and interesting. Wireless connected play to a powerful PC is also well done, but currently the included Wireless Adapter is not fully compatible with the Steam Machine – a baffling limitation we were shocked to confirm. VR is an expensive sub-hobby within video games, but Steam Frame is among the best ways to explore and enjoy it. $1059

Many of the coolest “gaming lights” focus on the flexibility and fun of bright RGB customization. While we’re fans of that aesthetic, it leaves others out in the cold who might want something a bit more natural. The Elements hex panels feature a natural wood-inspired panel, customizable “scenes” like a campfire glow, and can react to both music and touch, with adjustable ambient white light to keep the vibe relaxed. $200

#4266. KRÜ Blaze win Game Changers Championship from lower bracket, ending Gentle Mates’ unbeaten run

KRÜ Blaze came through the lower bracket to beat Europe's Gentle Mates GC over five maps in São Paulo, giving LATAM its first Game Changers Championship title. They are also the last winners of the standalone event, as next year's final moves to Champions.

KRÜ Blaze are the 2026 VALORANT Game Changers Championship winners. They edged Gentle Mates GC 3-2 at the Riot Games Arena in São Paulo on 1 November. No Latin American team had lifted the title before. No team had ever won it from the lower bracket either.

The event ran from 22 October, with 10 teams competing. Gentle Mates earned US$100,000 as runners-up. Shopify Rebellion Gold took US$70,000 for third place and MIBR GC US$50,000 for fourth.

KRÜ took the long route. They beat Gen.G GC 2-1 in the upper-bracket quarter-finals on 23 October. A 2-0 loss to Shopify Rebellion Gold on 27 October then dropped them into the lower bracket. They answered with clean sweeps of Team Liquid Brazil and MIBR GC. On 31 October they beat Shopify Rebellion Gold 3-1 in the best-of-five lower-bracket final.

The grand final swung back and forth. Gentle Mates took Haven 13-5 before KRÜ levelled on Abyss by the same score. KRÜ led the third map 10-2 at half-time. Gentle Mates fought back, but KRÜ closed it out 14-12 in overtime. Gentle Mates then won Split 13-8 to force a decider. KRÜ led 11-5 on Ascent and won it by the same margin as Split.

Liquipedia named KRÜ’s Argentine player tok1o as the event’s MVP. Brazilian teammates antG and none became the first Brazilians to win an international tournament held in São Paulo.

The result breaks a pattern. Before 2026 the title went to G2 Gozen for Europe in 2022, Shopify Rebellion for North America in 2023 and 2024, and Team Liquid Brazil in 2025. KRÜ’s own record at the event had improved steadily. They finished 7th–8th in 2022 and 5th–6th in each of the next two years. Last year they came fourth.

For European fans, it was a painful near miss. Gentle Mates GC arrived as EMEA’s top seed on circuit points. The team had not lost a series in São Paulo before the final, according to Esports News UK.

It capped a strong debut season in the circuit. Gentle Mates won EMEA Stage 1 by sweeping G2 Gozen 3-0 on 22 February. They lost the Stage 2 final to SK Nebula on 24 May without winning a map. On 30 August they lost the Stage 3 final to G2 Gozen in a fifth map. Silver in São Paulo leaves them with one title from four finals this year.

After a lower bracket run in São Paulo, the LATAM squad claimed the #VCTGameChangers Championship trophy! pic.twitter.com/YeSeb10TZc

— VCT Pacific (@vctpacific) November 1, 2026

The São Paulo final also closes a format. KRÜ are the last team to lift the trophy at a separate event of its own. For the first time, the Game Changers Championship will finish at Champions. Under Riot’s 2027 plan, non-partner teams that qualify for the Game Changers Championship will receive an extra US0,000 incentive. VALORANT Champions 2027 is scheduled for 16 September to 10 October in Austin.

#4262. After 15 years, The Sims' best spin-off finally gets its due follow-up in The Sims 4: Royalty & Legacy

The Sims Medieval had a short but powerful run back in 2011, and now many of its best features are finally coming to the main franchise.

The Sims 4 developers recently promised an exciting year for the game, and the franchise as a whole, and we just got an early look at one of those first events. After some light teasing, the developer unveiled Royalty & Legacy, the game’s next expansion.

Royalty & Legacy’s first trailer debuted on Thursday, revealing a February 12 release date, and showing off the expansion for the first time.

There’s a lot going on in Royalty & Legacy, which is priced $40. For one, it introduces a new world, Ondarion, which is going to be the setting for your kingdom, as you join a race for the throne. The expansion introduces Dynasty and Nobility - two new systems you can use to create your own world of royal shenanigans.

Ondarion is made up of three neighborhoods (regions). Each region has a unique theme and culture, and they’re each ruled by a Dynasty. Dambele is a place that prioritises art and community. Verdemar is a chaotic world of outlaws and nobles. Finally, Bellacorde is an extravagant region known for opulence and romance.

Speaking of building places, Royalty & Legacy also adds a new Lot type, The Backroom Lot. It serves two functions that change with the time of day. For instance, it can be a library or gym in the morning, and shift into a night club at night. Dambele has its own library-turned-rave, for instance.

At the heart of Ondarion are all the possible fantasy lives and stories you can live. The Sims calls them Powershifts, and they include some well-known Arthurian fantasies and other, more silly ones.

Swordsmanship is the new 10-level skill arriving with the expansion, which further plays into those fantasies by letting your Sims duel. There are even Swordsmanship Tournaments you can watch take place across every neighborhood in Ondarion.

Then there are Secret Passageways, which let you speed up moving across the new regions. They essentially let your Sims teleport between designated passageways, either on their own lots, or other lots in the world. Some of these are hidden for you to find, while others you can create.

In terms of new careers, there’s the Noble Career, where your Sim can rise through several Noble Rankings by doing basically what nobles had to do in the middle ages to earn favour.

The aforementioned Dynasty System is how you can join any of Ondarion’s existing families, or start your own. You actually have a lot of say in what goes on, including the usual business of appointing heirs.

Of course, no royal roleplay would be complete without scandals, which is where the Scandals System comes in. Through it, you can create stories to discredit others, or even topple an entire dynasty.

In November, you may recall The Sims 4 introducing new free items inspired by West African culture. In creating that content, EA worked with a group of Simmers who have direct ties to West African countries.

The group’s guidance was once again utilised to build the Dambele neighborhood in this expansion, and some of the lots around the world of Ondarion were even created by members of the group.

While you wait for Royalty & Legacy to actually arrive, there’s more in The Sims 4 you can jump in right now. The game recently kicked off a collaboration with fashion brand Coach that brought several free items to Create a Sim, and Build Buy. That arrived alongside a free update, which already makes for a busy start of the year for The Sims 4.

#4260. PlayStation 5 Crosses Major Sales Milestone Ahead of GTA 6 Launch

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

If ever there were a definitively good time to invest in a game console like the PlayStation 5, it’d certainly be now, what with the looming release of Grand Theft Auto 6 in just a little over a week. I can’t speak to how many people have gone out and bought PS5s for the express purpose of playing that game, but considering it's the console's best-selling title, I have to imagine it’s more than a few, and coupling those with the players who have already invested in the PS5 since its initial release in 2020, the overall statistics are nothing to sneeze at.

According to newly-released sales statistics from Sony Interactive Entertainment, as of yesterday, November 10, 2026, the PlayStation 5 has officially surpassed 100 million units sold worldwide in its lifespan.

For six years out from launch, that’s pretty good, especially since it’s a stone’s throw from the approximately 102 million-unit record held by the original PlayStation console, though it is a very far cry from the over-160 million PlayStation 2s sold. Hey, it was literally one of the best-selling game consoles of all time, anyone would have trouble beating that.

Rockstar says GTA 6 pre-loading begins November 10 and could require up to 212 GB, though some official pages still show the old date.

According to Sony’s sales statistics, in Q1 and Q2 2026 combined, about 3.2 million PS5 units have been sold. For the record, the console’s all-time quarterly sales record was set in Q3 2024 at 9.5 million, and the all-time yearly record was set in 2023 at 20.8.

Incidentally, these sales statistics are based on “sell-in” units, which means the numbers sold to officially licensed resellers, i.e. regular stores you buy gaming hardware at. The statistics don’t cover the sell-through numbers, which is the number of consoles actually purchased from resellers by end users. Presumably, that number is smaller, but if retailers are ordering lots of PS5s, it means people are buying them in large quantities, so that still says a lot.

In Q1 and Q2 2026 combined, about 3.2 million PS5 units have been sold.

The statistics don’t yet have the sales numbers for consoles in Q3, which lasts from October to December, but I have a hunch that, with the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 this month, those numbers are going to see at least some degree of lurch when they’re finally divulged. The stats sheet also doesn’t cover Q3’s software sales, but you can bet those are going to see a major hike for the same reason.

Take-Two has had an absolutely killer Q2, leading them to feed GTA fever more and more.

Despite how good all of these stats seem on paper, the reality of the situation is that the PS5’s overall sales for this year haven’t been especially hot. Comparing Q1 and Q2 statistics to years’ prior, both are smaller than every year from 2021 to 2025.

Granted, as I said, there is a nonzero chance we’re going to see a major lurch in the Q3 statistics; Q3, being the holiday season, usually sees a big jump every year, with sales doubling their usual rates from 2022 to 2025. With the once-in-a-generation winds of GTA 6 at its back, the PS5 could certainly recoup its failings in Q3 2026, though everyone who already has a PS5 or chooses to play that game elsewhere could hamper that projection.

Putting aside sales in 2020 and 2021, which were obviously hampered due to the COVID pandemic, it does seem like PS5 sales definitively peaked in 2023, and have been on a downswing since, with the primary suspected culprit being the console’s repeated price hikes and the gradual increase in cost of gaming as a hobby in the last couple of years.

Then again, it could just be that the PS5 is coming to the end of its time, and it’s time for the PS6 to take the reins, though in the current climate, it’s anyone’s guess how much that thing will end up costing.

Anyone in the United States of America who wants to get a PS5 for cheap needs to act fast, as the prices of all consoles are going up on August 21.

#4259. Void/Breaker Review – Chaos Is The Point

Many games tout impressive destruction systems under the hood, but few implement it as well as Void/Breaker. The ruin is visually spectacular, sure – who doesn’t love to watch buildings crumble because of your grenade or gravity-thrown explosives? But importantly, it’s a critical aspect of Void/Breaker’s roguelite design. Enemies caught beneath falling rubble become instantly staggered, and that’s your moment to kill. Grenades do this too, as do most items you throw at the hostile AI machinery trying to end your run, creating a vortex of shifting priorities as you dash, jump, and shoot at sequential staggered enemies in your sightlines. Countless weapon mods and permutations make fewer than a dozen weapons feel like hundreds in your arsenal, adding even more blissful chaos to the mix. Though it can be difficult at times, if you can see through the literal remains of your destruction, one of the year’s most engaging shooters awaits.

Void/Breaker wastes no time getting a gun in your hand. An AI voice in your head wants your help escaping a simulation where thousands of runners attempt to reach the end of multi-arena stages to defeat a boss. He asks that you simply follow the simulation’s commands; meanwhile, he uses the data you collect along the way to find new exits for you and him. The storytelling style is very reminiscent of Valve’s Portal. Something much larger is at play here, but it’s worth discovering for yourself.

This narrative framework supports the game’s roguelite structure. Mechanically, however, you enter various themed digital stages, from liminal spaces to beaches to snow-capped cliffs and more, and attempt to survive. Most arenas consist of a couple of starkly white structures that your grenades and thrown explosives can topple (ideally onto waves of enemies below). Learning the language of Void/Breaker means constantly scanning your field of view for explosives and structures practically begging to come down, and then eyeing neon-green bars above enemies that tell you they’re staggered and ready for a quick kill. Developer Stubby Games throws plenty of wrenches into this formula, like armored foes and electrostatic enemies you must melee first, and elite bots that will have you on the back foot, but for the most part, Void/Breaker’s formula is “Break stuff, then kill.”

The game emphasizes explosives and bringing buildings down, but your guns do most of the killing; you can only select one weapon per run. You choose from a pistol, shotgun, machine gun, sniper, and more, and each has its perks (though once I unlocked the SMG, I rarely picked anything else). There’s no sense overthinking your weapon, though, because the dozens of mods you pick up each run determine its effectiveness. As you pick up more schematics, the pool of mods you find in chests or drop from enemies expands, and soon your gun fires corrosive acid, electricity, fire, projectile missiles, and more. Not to mention, mods change how the gun fires, how much damage certain bullets do, recoil, accuracy, and just about any other stat you associate with firing a video game gun. Wild combinations are easy to create, and a unique mod-stacking mechanic that can double or triple effectiveness adds a light touch of puzzle design to this otherwise straight shooter.

Stubby Games smartly emphasizes player expression, never getting in the way of the zanier combinations available to players. The SMG I used to beat the final boss featured mods that made each bullet electric, shot missiles with each shot, covered each bullet in a destructive orb, and featured a ricochet perk that made each bullet bounce off walls and split into even more bullets. I’m thankful for mid-run saves because this SMG permutation, paired with an ability mod that let me throw infinite grenades for a limited time, filled my screen with so much destruction that the entire game crashed. I’d usually bemoan such a thing, but I couldn’t help but laugh. I pushed my PC to its limit with my on-screen chaos.

Boss fights leave a little to be desired – I rarely died because of their simple bullet-hell arenas. Instead, most runs ended because, after bringing down every structure around me, I’d get so lost in the chaos that I wouldn't realize I was stuck in debris while enemies swarmed my location. As stunning as it is to see so much happening on screen, it can be hard to understand what is going on during the most chaotic moments.

Between enemy-filled arenas en route to a stage’s end boss, you might find a shop to buy more mods, ominous obelisks with risk-reward propositions (gain a lot of health or lose half your health, for example), optional trials, and strange phenomena that transport you to different locations. These moments are quick breaks in between bouts of adrenaline-fueled shooter action that I always welcomed – enemies can be relentless, especially as new types are introduced in each stage.

The rest of the Void/Breaker package offers few genre surprises. You can upgrade various traits between runs, research new mod schematics to add to the random pool, purchase new weapons, and discover fun secrets. You can unlock shortcuts, glean in-world information from computer terminals, and hear intriguing dialogue barks from the AI partner who needs your help. It’s all standard stuff for the rogue genre, but if anything, its simplicity pushes you back to the meat and potatoes of this shooter.

Void/Breaker’s shorter runtime – I rolled credits at 12 hours – ensures nothing gets too repetitive in its roguelite structure, but an expansive endgame promises even more to engage with, like different run modifications you can enable to make an already chaotic shooter even more anarchic. I’ll certainly be running it back (again and again) to see what other disruptions I can bring to this AI-simulated adventure. It’s hard not to when destruction feels this good.

Invictus Gaming are through to the last four of Worlds 2026. They beat fellow LPL side Top Esports in the opening match of the Knockout Stage. The series was played at the Credit Union of Texas Event Center in Allen, Texas, on 3 November (US time).

The win guarantees China a semi-final place. That matters after the LPL’s 0-4 start in the Swiss Stage. IG now meet either Gen.G or LYON. Gen.G beat IG 1-0 in the Swiss Stage and finished it with a perfect 3-0 record.

TES played the event without ZUIAN. On 6 October the club announced that Bai ‘369’ Jia-Hao would move into the starting line-up because of visa problems affecting ZUIAN.

The stand-in still made his mark. IG won Game 1 after building a gold lead of more than 10,000. TES levelled in Game 2 when 369, on Renekton, killed JiaQi and TheShy on his own late in the game. IG then took the next two games to close out the series.

Every Knockout Stage match is a single-elimination best-of-five played with Fearless Draft. The two sides knew each other well. They met twice in best-of-five series in September. IG won 3-2 in the LPL Split 3 playoffs on 5 September. TES won 3-1 in the LPL Regional Finals on 17 September.

The prize money gap is now fixed. Worlds 2026 has a total prize pool of US$5,000,000, with US$1,000,000 for the winner. Each losing semi-finalist receives US$400,000, so IG are guaranteed at least that sum.

IG’s run began with a mid-season rescue. The team started LPL Split 3 in the Nirvana Group. The club then asked TheShy and Rookie, who were both on a break, to come back. The pair helped the side qualify for Worlds. Both won the 2018 world title with IG.

TheShy said he had promised IG’s CEO he would help if asked. “I came back to keep my word,” he said after the series.

The semi-finals will be played in Allen on 7 and 8 November. The final will be held in Brooklyn on Saturday 14 November at 2pm EST.

#4255. Tomorrow's Battlefield 6 patch somehow makes jets more useless, improves armor bar visibility in Redsec

The first Battlefield 6 patch of the year is almost here, bringing a smattering of changes, including one that doesn't quite make sense.

Battlefield 6’s promised, season-extending update has been officially detailed. The patch, version 1.1.3.5, arrives tomorrow, January 20 right when Season 1 was supposed to end. Part of the update’s goal is to extend the current season, until Season 2 kicks off in the middle of February.

Update 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.

Patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller update. When Battlefield Studios announced it earlier last week, the developer didn’t promise any major changes or fixes, so expectations never got out of hand.

The patch is mainly made up of bug fixes, but it does have three key areas of improvements to gameplay. There’s a big focus on melee combat, how responsive/unresponsive it is with the various melee tools, and how melee behaviour interacts with sprinting and other animations.

The end result should be faster attack speeds for the knife, and clearer wind-up animations for both the knife and the sledgehammer. The timing dictating when melee damage gets credited has also been made more consistent in different environments.

Interestingly, sprint is now only interrupted when the melee attack reaches its target. As it stands, sprinting is only interrupted after the full duration of the animation has been completed, which adds to the that perceived feeling of sluggishness.

The other major, and arguably most confusing is the nerf to jet cannons. The patch is going to make jets far less stronger against other air vehicles, requiring 40% more hits to destroy a target. This is puzzling because jets - and air vehicles in general - are already the least survivable in Battlefield 6.

And, considering how the rest of a jet's arsenal is either situational or nearly ineffective, the cannons were really the one guaranteed way of downing other air vehicles, so long as you manage to land your shots consistently. While the change is wellmeaning, the percentage will likely be reduced in future patches.

Finally, the update makes a few refinements to UI across the game, though mainly aimed at Redsec and modes where players wear armor. Armor bar visibility has been improved, and there’s a fix for the annoying bug that sometimes caused the armor bar to disappear every few seconds.

As promised, Battlefield Labs is coming back to bring us a preview of some of Battlefield 6’s upcoming Season 2 content.

Battlefield 6’s Season 2 was recently pushed back by a month to give Battlefield Studios time to polish up its content. Now, the developer has revealed how it plans to use some of that time, and the first port of call is Battlefield Labs.

As discussed in the initial delay message, BF Studios wants the community’s involvement earlier and more consistently in the development of future content. This includes Season 2, of course, and a big component of what it’s bringing to the game is headed to Labs.

The first Battlefield Labs session kicking off soon will focus on Contaminated, one of the new maps coming to Battlefield 6 with Season 2. BF Studios says the map falls between Eastwood and Mirak Valley, in terms of size.

The blog post even likened it to Battlefield 1’s St. Quentin Scar, and Battlefield 5’s Arras. Although we’ve yet to actually play it, the size and description do sound really well, especially in a game as starved of big maps as Battlefield 6 currently is.

Another thing BF Studios wants to test is the way ground vehicle gameplay and aerial presence interact with infantry combat, which is pretty standard for most Battlefield maps. #4251. Double Fine Is Updating a Game With Almost No Players on Steam, And We’re Just as Confused

Covering the video games industry since 2017, with experience in news, articles, and reviews. Currently a writer at DualShockers and gaming magazines.

It truly is more admirable to watch a developer who never gives up on a project, even when things aren't exactly going according to plan. But sometimes, I have to wonder if a little stubbornness is involved, too – and that's pretty much how I feel about Double Fine's latest announcement, as the studio has just revealed an update for a game that can barely keep anyone playing on Steam.

The game in question is Kiln, a rather unusual multiplayer title that launched earlier this year. And while I certainly appreciate developers continuing to support their games after release, announcing a major content update for a title that regularly has almost zero players online is certainly an interesting decision. So, what exactly is Double Fine planning here?

For those who might have missed it, Kiln is a multiplayer party brawler developed by Double Fine Productions, the studio behind the beloved Psychonauts franchise. Its premise is pretty unusual: players use a pottery wheel to create their own ceramic fighters, with the size and shape of each pot determining their abilities and playstyle during team-based battles.

It's a genuinely creative concept, and one that sounds like it could lead to some pretty chaotic matches with friends. Unfortunately, the game hasn't managed to attract a particularly large audience since its April 23 launch.

Double Fine Productions has released its game, Keeper, on PlayStation 5, after the port was highly requested by fans.

According to SteamDB, Kiln reached an all-time peak of just 193 concurrent players on Steam, and its numbers have been considerably lower ever since. At the time of writing, the game currently has only one player online, with its 24-hour peak sitting at just 13. That's not exactly the kind of multiplayer community you'd hope to see for a game built entirely around online matches.

Still, Double Fine doesn't seem ready to throw in the towel. The studio has announced Kiln: Reshaped, a major update arriving on November 12 for PC and consoles, bringing a handful of new features that might give players a reason to return.

At the time of writing, the game currently has only one player online, with its 24-hour peak sitting at just 13.

Basically, this upcoming update will introduce two new online modes, along with a local co-op multiplayer option called “Mini Quench”. That's not all, either, as players will also get access to a brand-new Photobooth in the game’s hub, allowing them to pose their ceramic creations and take screenshots with friends. Double Fine also promises plenty of additional decorations and more content, although the full patch notes (which you can read here) will only arrive alongside the update.

The addition of kernel-level anti-cheat last week has resulted in a fresh campaign of outrage against Helldivers 2.

Interestingly, the studio is also turning the launch into a little community celebration called “Day of Clay”. Double Fine is inviting everyone to jump into Kiln on November 12 after 10:30 AM PT, with the possibility of running into some members of the development team during matchmaking. And honestly, I kind of love that idea! There's something charming about a developer wanting to spend time with the remaining players rather than simply moving on to the next project.

Of course, whether these additions will be enough to bring Kiln back to life is another question entirely, but I’m certain that at least one player is extremely happy today! Also, it is worth remembering that Steam numbers don't tell the whole story, especially when the game is also available on consoles, so its community is probably bigger than that.

For now, Double Fine seems determined to keep its pottery brawler spinning. Let's just hope there are enough players around to actually enjoy all that new content.

Tim Schafer still believes that Game Pass could be a positive for smaller devs seeking to get their games into the public eye.

Gen.G swept LYON in the second Worlds 2026 quarter-final in Allen, Texas. The defeat removes North America’s last team from the tournament. The LCK top seed now face Invictus Gaming in a best-of-five semi-final on Saturday, starting at 16:00 Central Time.

Reaching the last four secures Gen.G at least third or fourth place. That is a familiar stopping point for the organisation. It has finished third or fourth at four of its last five Worlds and has never played in a Worlds final, GosuGamers reported.

The stakes go beyond one team. Gen.G entered the tournament as the LCK’s top seed. Korean sides are chasing a fifth Summoner’s Cup in a row.

Their opponents bring their own history. Invictus Gaming beat Top Esports 3-1 in the opening quarter-final. That put iG into their first Worlds semi-final since 2019. TheShy and Rookie, who won Worlds with iG in 2018, are back in the last four.

The money rises sharply from here. Worlds 2026 carries a US$5,000,000 prize pool. The champion takes US$1,000,000 (20%), and the runner-up receives US$800,000.

For LYON, the exit still marks clear progress. They go out in joint fifth to eighth place and collect a share of the prize money. GosuGamers called it easily the organisation’s best Worlds finish. In four earlier appearances, LYON never placed higher than 17th.

Their elimination also changes the shape of the event. North America will have no representative in the semi-finals or the Grand Final. The remaining matches in Allen will be contested without a team from the region.
